problem: Open-vocabulary robot navigation methods rely on SLAM, map construction, reinforcement learning or large prior observations (EmbodiedQA, LM-Nav, VLMaps, CLIP-Fields), so a real robot cannot start operating immediately in an unknown environment. Classic reflex-based navigation, in turn, only handles coordinate goals and collision avoidance, not language.
motivation: The paper wants the simplest possible navigation with no map, no learning and no prior knowledge. An omnidirectional camera sees all directions at once, so no exploratory behavior or trajectory generation is needed. CLIP and Detic each fail on different kinds of instructions, so combining them should make direction choice more robust.
key_idea: Split an expanded 360° image into N sectors, score each sector against the instruction with CLIP (global) and Detic+Sentence-BERT (local), multiply the two scores, and reflexively drive toward the weighted-average best direction.
insight: CLIP judges the whole image and confuses related concepts (microwave vs kitchen), while Detic judges individual objects and misses scene-level instructions. Multiplying the normalized scores compensates for both. In the basic experiment the combined method ALL was best overall, while CLIP alone drove toward the kitchen for the 'microwave' instruction and Detic alone meandered. Modifiers in the instruction (wooden table, bookshelf) were needed to disambiguate similar objects, and an unseen target (microwave) was reached by first heading toward the kitchen where it is usually found.
method: Omnidirectional image: dual-fisheye images from an Insta360 Air are corrected for intensity, unwarped, aligned and blended into a 2000x1000 image, then cropped to 2000x500 (image V) to remove ceiling and robot head.

Image splitting + VLMs: V is split into N_split=8 possibly overlapping pieces. CLIP encodes each piece. Detic (LVIS classes) runs once on the full V and its result is split; labels sorted by bbox size are joined into a sentence and encoded by Sentence-BERT.
Similarity scoring: cosine similarity of each sector with the instruction (CLIP text embedding, or Sentence-BERT embedding), min-max normalized to [0.1,1] as a_i^clip and a_i^detic.
Score fusion: e_i = a_i^clip * a_i^detic. The 0.1 floor keeps e_i nonzero when one model scores very low.
Direction computation: take the top N_extract sectors by e_i and average their direction vectors b_i with rank weights (N_extract+1-j). This avoids local minima from picking only the argmax.
Reflex control: for a two-wheeled base, linear speed is 1.0 if |θ|<C_thre (0.6 rad) and rotation is kθ (k=0.5), run at 10 Hz. Fetch's LRF blocks motion toward obstacles.
Runtime: CLIP runs at up to 12 Hz and Detic at 5 Hz (i7-6850K, RTX 3090). CLIP time grows with N_split, Detic time does not.

setting.observation: 360° omnidirectional RGB (dual fisheye, Insta360 Air) plus LRF for obstacle blocking
setting.action_space: continuous base velocity (linear 1.0 m/s, rotation kθ) at 10 Hz

numbers_note: Basic-experiment results (5 runs per instruction for ALL, CLIP, Detic; final position error) are given only as trajectory plots and an error graph in figures, with no numeric table. The advanced experiment is qualitative. No standard benchmark is used.
results: In a 2.5x1.6 m enclosure with three instructions (kitchen, microwave, desk), the combined ALL method had the best overall final-position error and trajectories. CLIP alone failed on 'microwave' by heading to the kitchen, and Detic alone meandered. In a larger space the robot handled a chain of three changing instructions, distinguishing a TV on a wooden table from monitors on a white desk, and reached the microwave by first going toward the kitchen.
limitations: Manually tuned parameters (N_split, overlap), and a trade-off between accuracy and inference time.
Inherits VLM weaknesses: ambiguous instructions cause the robot to spin, negation is not understood, and accuracy depends on object size.
Fails in concave or complex spaces, since there is no memory or exploration. Evaluation is small-scale and qualitative, with no standard benchmark or baseline navigation methods.
